title: NASA Wants Your Big Idea for Living on the Moon!
summary: Have you ever imagined what it would be like to live on the Moon? NASA is asking college students to come up with amazing ideas for how we could live and work there in the future. It's part of a competition called RASC-AL, which stands for Revolutionary Aerospace Systems Concepts - Academic Linkage. That's a fancy name for a challenge where students design new technology for space. This year, the theme is all about the Moon's South Pole. That's a super interesting place because some craters there are always in shadow. It's super cold, but there might be ice hidden there! Students are asked to think of ways to explore those dark craters, find resources, and build things that future astronauts will need. It's like a giant puzzle for future space explorers. Teams from universities all over the United States can join. They have to send in their ideas by February 24, 2027. Up to 14 teams will be chosen to go to Florida in June 2027 to present their ideas to NASA experts. Each finalist team gets $7,500 to help them. The top two teams get even more money and a chance to show their idea at a big space conference. So if you love space and building things, maybe one day you could be part of a team like this. The Moon is waiting for your ideas!
why_it_matters: This contest shows that young people's creative ideas matter, and if you love space and building things, you could one day help people live on the Moon.

background_read: NASA has been planning to send astronauts back to the Moon through its Artemis program.
The Moon's South Pole has deep craters where sunlight never reaches, so water ice could stay frozen underground.
Student competitions like RASC-AL help space agencies hear fresh ideas while students get to practice real engineering.
Article_Structure: WHO: College students from universities across the United States are invited to join NASA's RASC-AL competition.
WHAT: They must create ideas for living and working on the Moon's South Pole, exploring dark craters and finding resources.
WHERE: Finalist teams will travel to Florida in June 2027 to present their ideas to NASA experts.
WHY: NASA wants new technology that will help future astronauts live and work on the Moon.

perspectives.description: NASA sees the competition as a way to find fresh ideas for future Moon missions.
Students see it as a chance to get real experience, travel to Florida, and win money for their teams.
They know the Moon's South Pole is promising because of ice, but exploring dark craters is very difficult and needs new designs.
